A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same egocentric instruction-tuning study and EgoOrientBench. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, response-type ablations, confusion matrices, pedestrian examples, and spatial-reasoning results, including supplementary results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations on MMStar, MMMU, and POPE in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same eight orientation classes, three instruction-response types, and LoRA tuning of the language model and bridge with a frozen visual encoder. Appendix data-generation prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 add actual evaluations on MMStar, MMMU, and POPE, substantially broadening general-performance coverage beyond MME, including multidisciplinary reasoning and object hallucination. Training data, EgoOrientBench coverage, pedestrian examples, and COCO-Spatial evaluation are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same models and baselines: Popular, zero-shot backbones, Gemini-1.5, and GPT-4o in Table 1, and zero-shot versus tuned versions of the same three backbones in Table 2. The added benchmarks introduce no new comparators.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported metric set from MME Perception, Cognition, and Total to aggregate MME plus MMStar, MMMU, and POPE scores. Existing model sizes, training settings, and EgoOrientBench procedures remain unchanged; detailed protocols for the added benchmarks are not supplied.

E4.justification: The response-type ablations, confusion matrices, pedestrian case study, spatial-reasoning analysis, and articulated-object error examples are unchanged, including Appendix C. The additional general-benchmark scores introduce no new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantive results on three general benchmarks for all three backbones. Newly reported zero-shot/tuned scores include LLaVA-1.5 POPE at 82.03/88.36 and InternVL2 MMStar at 54.26/53.13, showing mixed effects. MME totals remain identical, but its Perception/Cognition entries are removed. Other experimental results, including appendix ablations, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The orientation definitions and conceptual method description are unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theoretical results, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that consistent egocentric instruction tuning improves orientation understanding while preserving general capabilities, and introduce the same benchmark. The conclusion references broader supporting benchmarks without changing the underlying contribution or claim.

C2.justification: The annotation-inconsistency explanation, bias-mitigation interpretation, and limitations involving conflicting head/body orientations and discrete categories are retained. Section 5.2 applies the existing general-capability-preservation interpretation to additional results; the rewritten limitations add no substantive qualification.

D1.justification: Hardware, training duration, learning rates, LoRA settings, batch information, data processing, rendering instructions, evaluator prompts, and project access information are retained. The added benchmarks receive no corresponding implementation or reproduction details.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MMStar, MMMU, and POPE references and removes LLaVA-Docent, ShapeLLM, and Lumos when shortening Section 4.1. The central positioning relative to earlier orientation-understanding work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the dataset description, general-performance discussion, limitations, and conclusion. It adds 'Large' to the title, updates author information, and adds acknowledgments. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 is reformatted from MME category/total columns into four benchmark columns, with a revised caption. Local spacing and text reflow change page composition, while the other figures and table structures, including those in the appendices, are retained.

improvement.justification: The expanded Table 2 provides broader evidence for the existing claim that orientation tuning preserves general capabilities, previously supported only by MME. This is a limited improvement: the method and primary results are unchanged, MME category detail is lost, and the added evaluations lack detailed protocols and uncertainty reporting.
